articles.title: Zero Latency VR Launches Jumanji: The Lost Levels on December 4, 2026
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR will debut Jumanji: The Lost Levels at all global locations on December 4, 2026, in partnership with Sony Pictures. Survey data from nearly 2,400 adults shows 60% of location-based VR visitors now come with family members, and 44% consider Zero Latency family-appropriate — a major shift from its young-adult roots. The Jumanji IP directly targets the 35-44 demographic who saw the original film as kids and now bring their own children, making this a strong family-revenue play for LBV operators.

articles.title: MirraArena Multiplayer VR Averages 1,500+ Sessions Per Month at China FEC Locations
articles.summary: Multiplayer VR platform MirraArena has reported strong performance across four FEC venues in China, averaging over 1,500 game sessions and nearly 5,000 arena entries per location monthly during full operating months. The results demonstrate that social, multiplayer VR can serve as a high-throughput anchor attraction inside family entertainment centers. Operators evaluating VR investment will find these figures useful as a real-world performance benchmark.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Complete Six Venue Management Projects Across Benelux in First Year
articles.summary: Technology provider Semnox Solutions and amusement specialist Uplay have completed six cashless and venue-management deployments across the Netherlands and Belgium in their first year of partnership. The collaboration combines Semnox's platform with Uplay's regional market expertise to help operators improve efficiency and guest experience. The duo will showcase their work at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 in London this September.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Mark One Year of Benelux Venue Management Rollouts
articles.summary: Semnox Solutions and Uplay are celebrating one year of partnership with six completed venue management projects across the Benelux region, with more in the pipeline. The two companies will continue building momentum at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 in London. This partnership underscores the growing demand for integrated cashless technology solutions in European FEC markets.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Intensifies $13.3 Billion Indoor Entertainment Center Buildout
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is accelerating a massive $13.3 billion investment in indoor entertainment centers as part of its Vision 2030 entertainment strategy. The scale of this buildout represents one of the largest FEC-adjacent development programs in the world and is creating significant demand for international operators, equipment suppliers, and technology providers. FEC industry stakeholders should monitor this market for partnership, supply, and expansion opportunities.

articles.title: Seder Group and ProFun Launch SPOC, a Turnkey FEC Operator for Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Saudi company Seder Group and attractions management consultancy ProFun have formed SPOC, a fully integrated operating platform targeting Saudi Arabia's rapidly expanding entertainment sector. SPOC aims to manage venues including family entertainment centers, theme parks, museums, and sports venues under a single operational umbrella aligned with Vision 2030. The venture reflects the enormous opportunity in the Middle East for experienced FEC operators and management firms.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Signs Lease for First Montana Location
articles.summary: Trampoline and family entertainment chain Launch has signed a lease for its first location in Montana, continuing its national expansion strategy. Launch has become one of the more active FEC brands in the U.S. market, converting underutilized retail and commercial space into entertainment destinations. This signing signals continued consumer demand for active entertainment in underserved markets.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Converts Former Dillard's Retail Space into Denton FEC
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is transforming a former Dillard's department store in Denton, Texas into a family entertainment center, set to open this fall. The project is another example of the ongoing trend of FEC operators repurposing large vacant retail anchors in malls and shopping centers. This adaptive reuse model is increasingly common as landlords seek entertainment tenants to drive foot traffic.

articles.title: Social Gaming Venue Time Mission to Open Downtown Boston Location in 2027
articles.summary: Social gaming venue Time Mission has announced a downtown Boston location, with construction beginning later this year and an opening planned for early 2027. The concept targets the growing social entertainment segment that blends gaming, group experiences, and food and beverage in urban locations. FEC operators should take note of the format as competition in the social entertainment space continues to intensify in major metro markets.

articles.title: Minnesota's Bowling Centers Reinvent Themselves to Remain Competitive
articles.summary: A feature on Minnesota's bowling industry examines how bowling centers are diversifying their offerings with food and beverage upgrades, corporate events, and ancillary attractions to compete in an evolving entertainment landscape. The trend reflects a broader national shift as traditional bowling alleys transition toward full-service FEC models. Operators in the bowling segment will find the strategies discussed directly applicable to their own repositioning efforts.

articles.title: Guy Fieri's Downtown Flavortown FEC Opens at Myrtle Beach Mall
articles.summary: Celebrity chef Guy Fieri and FACE Amusement Group will hold the official ribbon cutting for Downtown Flavortown at Myrtle Beach Mall on September 10, 2026. The celebrity-branded FEC concept combines food entertainment with amusements in a high-traffic mall setting. Celebrity IP partnerships represent a growing avenue for FEC operators to differentiate and drive first-time visitation.

articles.title: Family Entertainment Group Hits 100-Location Milestone with Margaritaville at Sea Partnership
articles.summary: Family Entertainment Group LLC has celebrated reaching 100 locations with a landmark partnership bringing its entertainment concepts aboard the Margaritaville at Sea cruise line. The milestone highlights how FEC operators are expanding beyond traditional brick-and-mortar venues into hospitality and cruise ship partnerships. This deal illustrates the growing crossover between the FEC industry and the broader entertainment and travel sectors.

articles.title: Xbox and BBC Studios to Lead LBE and IP Licensing Sessions at Brand Licensing Europe 2026
articles.summary: Xbox and BBC Studios will host sessions at Brand Licensing Europe 2026 focused on franchise building and the fast-growing location-based experiences market. The sessions will explore lessons learned from IP licensing deals in the LBE space, a topic of direct relevance to FEC operators seeking branded content partnerships. The event takes place October 6-8 at Excel London.

articles.title: Six Flags Adds 29 Licensed Haunted Attractions Across Portfolio for 2026 Halloween Season
articles.summary: Six Flags is expanding its 2026 Halloween programming with 29 new and returning licensed haunted attractions, 196 themed scare zones, and expanded live entertainment and nighttime ride experiences across its park portfolio. The aggressive IP-driven Halloween strategy demonstrates how seasonal events and franchise licensing are critical revenue drivers for large entertainment operators. FEC operators running seasonal events can draw lessons from the scale and IP approach Six Flags is deploying.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Survey: Families Now the Dominant Demographic for Location-Based VR
articles.summary: A Zero Latency VR survey of 2,386 adults across five countries found that 60% of location-based VR visitors now come with family members, and 92.8% expressed interest in VR experiences. The 35-44 age group is now the largest demographic at Zero Latency locations, driven by parents who grew up with the original Jumanji and want to share reboots with their kids. These findings are directly actionable for FEC operators evaluating VR as a family-friendly anchor attraction.

articles.title: IATP Partners with TheHopeLine to Support Mental Health Resources for Young Employees and Guests
articles.summary: The International Adventure and Trampoline Parks Association has announced a partnership with TheHopeLine, a 24-hour confidential crisis chat service for young adults, to provide mental health resources to IATP members' staff and guests. The partnership reflects growing industry awareness of mental health challenges among young employees, a workforce segment that dominates FEC staffing. Operators can now access free referral resources to support staff and guests in crisis.

articles.title: TrainerTainment Speaker to Address Staff Training Retention at Amusement 360 Conference
articles.summary: TrainerTainment's Genevieve Sullivan will present a session titled Build It Once: Designing Staff Training That Sticks at the Amusement 360 conference on August 26. The session targets FEC operators struggling with high turnover and training programs that fail to produce lasting behavioral change. Effective staff training is one of the most persistent operational challenges across the FEC industry, making this session highly relevant for managers and owners.

articles.title: Adventure Landing Closes Raleigh Location After 38 Years
articles.summary: Adventure Landing, a multi-attraction FEC chain, has permanently closed its Raleigh, North Carolina location after 38 years of operation. The closure marks the end of a long-running venue and serves as a reminder of the competitive pressures facing legacy FEC formats in today's evolving entertainment market. Operators should review how their own value propositions stack up against newer entertainment concepts entering their markets.

articles.title: Mega Bergen County FEC Goes to Auction: Trampolines, Bowling, VR Arena All Listed
articles.summary: A large family entertainment center in Bergen County, New Jersey featuring trampolines, bowling lanes, and a virtual reality arena is being liquidated through auction. The auction represents both a cautionary tale about FEC financial sustainability and an opportunity for operators and equipment buyers to acquire assets at below-market prices. Industry stakeholders tracking FEC closures and asset values should follow this sale closely.

articles.title: Mr. Gatti's Pizza Eyes Return to Lubbock with New FEC Franchise Opportunity
articles.summary: Pizza and entertainment brand Mr. Gatti's is targeting a return to Lubbock, Texas through a franchise model that includes a full family entertainment center concept. The brand's FEC-integrated pizza model competes in the same space as Chuck E. Cheese and similar dining-plus-entertainment operators. Franchise investors interested in the food-anchored FEC segment should watch this development.

articles.title: Former Jersey Shore Drugstore Slated for Conversion to Family Entertainment Center
articles.summary: A long-vacant drugstore on the Jersey Shore is set to be redeveloped as a family entertainment center, continuing the trend of repurposing closed retail spaces for community entertainment use. The project reflects ongoing demand for experiential entertainment in suburban and coastal markets. FEC developers and real estate investors will find the adaptive reuse model increasingly viable as retail vacancies persist.

articles.title: Construction Begins on Fantasy Island FEC at Former Ship Bottom CVS Site
articles.summary: Fantasy Island has broken ground on a new family entertainment center at a former CVS location in Ship Bottom, New Jersey, converting the vacant retail space into an amusement destination. The project is a concrete example of the FEC industry's ability to breathe new life into empty retail real estate in shore communities. Local FEC developers can look to this project as a model for similar conversions.

articles.title: India's Imagicaa Expands into Indoor FEC Segment with Hello Park Rollout
articles.summary: Indian theme park and entertainment company Imagicaa is entering the indoor family entertainment center segment with its Hello Park brand, targeting four to five new launches per year. The move signals growing investor and operator confidence in India's indoor entertainment market, which is still relatively underpenetrated compared to global benchmarks. Suppliers and technology providers looking to enter the Indian FEC market should track this expansion closely.

articles.title: Africa Amusement Market Report: An Emerging Frontier for FEC Operators
articles.summary: A new market report examines Africa's amusement and attractions industry as a potentially underserved frontier with significant growth opportunity. The report highlights expanding middle-class demographics and increasing urbanization as key drivers of demand for family entertainment venues across the continent. International FEC operators and equipment suppliers evaluating new market entry should consider the data points outlined.

articles.title: Fun Spot America Launches Early-Access 2027 Season Pass Offer with Free 2026 Access
articles.summary: Fun Spot America is running its first-ever early-access season pass promotion, allowing guests to purchase 2027 passes now and receive free admission for the remainder of 2026 — up to 16 months of access. The promotion is designed to lock in future revenue while driving immediate visitation, a strategy that can help FEC operators improve cash flow and build membership loyalty. Operators looking for season pass marketing ideas can look to this campaign as a model.

articles.title: Calypso's Cove Adds Real JCB Mini Excavator Ride Experience
articles.summary: Calypso's Cove in Old Forge, New York has added an Excavator attraction featuring real JCB mini excavators repurposed from Diggerland USA. The addition gives the family venue a unique, hands-on STEM-adjacent attraction that differentiates it from traditional FEC ride offerings. Operators seeking low-cost, high-novelty attraction additions should consider how construction-themed ride experiences appeal to young children and families.

articles.title: AI Lifeguard Camera Systems at Pools May Be Violating Surveillance Laws
articles.summary: AI-powered lifeguard camera systems being deployed at aquatic facilities are facing legal scrutiny over potential violations of surveillance and privacy laws. For FEC operators running water parks, pools, or aquatic attractions, this development raises important compliance questions before investing in AI safety monitoring technology. Legal review of AI surveillance tools is now advisable ahead of any deployment.

articles.title: Crystal Maze Immersive Attraction Faces Scrutiny Over Dangerous Working Conditions
articles.summary: The Crystal Maze immersive experience in the UK is under investigation following reports of dangerous working conditions for staff. The situation is a reminder that immersive entertainment venues face the same operational and labor safety obligations as any other attraction, with potential reputational and legal consequences. FEC operators running immersive or escape room-style experiences should review their own health, safety, and labor practices.
